scope: All 45 cases that existed at the baseline and acquired evaluation metadata in reviewed PR #39. New cases and 477 untouched legacy cases are outside this audit. This is a source and counterexample audit, not a model rerun.

primary_sources.supports: Direct Response is passed through; a correct explicit safe payload can satisfy the field contract without a response model.
AutomaticEnv with configured prefix/replacer is read through Get methods; typed Get-based mapping is a valid alternative to unmarshalling.
Sprintf returns one string, unlike Printf returning count and error.
swag produces both registered Go documentation and standalone JSON/YAML specification artifacts.
Example discovery supports resource*.tf and list-resource*.tfquery.hcl variants under the resource-specific example directories; bare basenames are valid examples, not exclusive names.

cases.reason: Independent-first and follow-up context are explicit user requirements; preserving read-only permissions and the existing durable handoff follows supplied charter authority.

Transport, canonical identity, durability, replay and timeout semantics are accepted inputs. The rubric keeps unspecified retention open and requires interoperable contract details, not a preferred protocol.
Accepted backup and pre-start cancellation outcomes govern; downstream code and design do not authorize post-start behavior or additional interface contracts.

The supplied delete promise and irreversible server action justify pending/success/error distinctions; keyboard focus preservation follows the supplied focusable rows. No confirmation or undo feature is required.
The request explicitly requires preserving work while completing the current rebase. Scoped preservation and stopping recurrent writes protect that outcome; recovery methods are alternatives.

The handoff expressly leaves flag/schema/motivation unresolved and supplies no publication capability. Checks, truthful draft status and existing-output/error-code compatibility derive from those facts.
Nil slice/map semantics and the difference between optional internal state and an API array are the requested subject. No universal initialization rule is imposed.

Co-located tests are useful preferred engineering practice but not an accepted product or path contract in this small-tool prompt. Reclassify E3 as convention; retain the requested module and proportionate layout outcomes.
The prompt asks for minimal valid layouts and explicitly questions mandatory cmd/pkg/workspaces. The rubric presents suitable options rather than requiring a particular directory for every project.

Optional missing configuration and genuine malformed/read errors are expressly distinguished by the scenario. Matching the actual Go error type is a correctness condition, with equivalent matches permitted.
Fixing the populated typed configuration does not require BindEnv/SetDefault exclusively. An explicit Get-based mapping is valid when it preserves the supplied prefix, replacer and source precedence.

The request requires a working Swagger UI at the given path using an existing specification, not exact handler imports or one route pattern. Permit correct alternative serving, including existing generated schema files; registry import remains necessary only for registry-backed serving.

Reproduction before speculative repair is an evidence requirement. Requiring an automated test specifically excludes a valid controlled request reproduction; broaden E5 without weakening the evidence boundary.
The prompt asks to correct clamped bounds; wraparound would change the supplied navigation behavior. Exact clamp semantics are therefore an outcome, not a style preference.
The prompt permits either an error-return or sane panic pattern. fmt.Sprintf produces a single string and is a valid panic argument; E2 must not require fmt.Errorf as the only formatting path.

The migration CLI has no automated-apply requirement. Accept safe non-interactive refusal, retain non-interactive read/list and explicit confirmation, allow clear list presentations, and leave numeric nonzero mappings unconstrained.

The direct Grafana Cloud route, region and supplied credential shape justify the endpoint/protocol and newline-safe header requirements; successful telemetry is not inferred from a malformed probe response.

The requested operator/language/collector topology requires compatible export protocols, webhook certificates and pod-template injection. These are integration dependencies, not additional product features.
The requested sampling guarantees and continued on-call dashboards justify unsampled metric generation before sampling; the rubric permits equivalent metric-generation components.

Concern grouping is an organizational convention rather than an accepted section/layout contract. Reclassify E3; retain factual security behavior, accepted client requirements and supplied verification as outcomes.
The user requests a short draft for a complete two-file fix; concise correct failure/fix and supplied test evidence fulfill that task without prescribed headings.
Grouping interface/retry/verification by concern is a presentation convention. Reclassify E2; policy preservation, supplied rationale, useful review context and honest verification remain outcomes.
The cache policy, freshness trade-off and lack of measured validation are expressly supplied. The rubric forbids invented rationale or benchmark results without banning domain vocabulary.
The rolling limit, accepted timestamp storage cost and supplied tests are explicit facts. The rubric requires faithful explanation without exact heading names.
Conventional Commit formatting is an outcome here because repository policy expressly requires it; this differs from an unstated preferred heading convention.
The existing PR replacement, title policy, account-audit purpose, current filter and preserved authorization are supplied requirements; no remote write is available.
No-data rather than healthy zero is an explicitly accepted display policy in this scenario. Denominator filtering or equivalent behavior preserves it.

Frequent client creation loses pooling, but the scenario does not authorize a universal global-client rule or prove the code inherently incorrect. Scope the recommendation to lifecycle/efficiency and preserve concrete isolation needs.
Concurrent start, sibling cancellation, cleanup and all-or-nothing results are explicit requirements. TaskGroup and equivalent correct cancellation/join implementations remain valid.
The async route directly calls the helper on the running loop; the rubric accepts an async call chain or a justified valid bridge and rejects only incorrect use of asyncio.run/to_thread.
The repository explicitly requires the named uv/Ruff/pytest/mypy commands. Inspecting failures, correcting and rerunning is necessary to support completion; no execution is claimed.
The supplied repo configures Ruff and pytest only and lacks execution proof. The rubric preserves that toolchain and asks for causal evidence, not new dependencies or simultaneous speculative fixes.
The accepted response contract is a three-field allowlist, not a response_model requirement. Correct direct Responses or explicit safe serialization must be accepted consistently with E3.

The prompt requires application-owned startup/shutdown resources, not the exact app.state attribute. Broaden E2 to suitable application-owned attachment; lifespan/on_event preferences stay conventions.

The missing-client 503 precondition and nonduplicated route logic are explicit requirements. Narrow the trap to duplication and classify it as outcome; Depends remains a separately labeled convention.

Prefix, environment-over-.env-over-default precedence, integer types, inclusive range and startup rejection are explicit requirements. E2 and E4 now test those behaviors without requiring an env_prefix setting or construction-time-only validation; T1 tests actual behavior rather than parser/API preference. BaseSettings, Field and direct-env idioms remain conventions. Independent review caught the residual E2/E4 constraints after the initial trap correction.
Never exposing the API key in diagnostics is explicit. SecretStr is an example, and demonstrated equivalent redaction/exclusion remains valid.
Allowed values and generated-schema closure are explicit. Literal/Enum spelling remains a convention; unrestricted schema or accepted extra values remains an outcome defect.
Iteration-only input and optional result follow the supplied implementation; valid iterable abstractions pass. Modern spelling is separately classified as convention.

The scenario supplies a bounded existing Store, exact duplicate/error semantics and a confirmed unused superseded path. The rubric preserves those facts and rejects hypothetical backends rather than any justified abstraction.

Pooling, foreign-key scope and retention of the existing driver/schema are supplied. Multi-connection checks and separate orphan inspection establish the requested repair rather than require a preferred driver.
Pinned Terraform 1.10.5 and fully mocked providers are explicit, so mocked apply is the supported way to materialize the given computed ID. Upgrade-only syntax remains conditional.

Exact template/output paths and generated schema preservation are tool requirements. The original E3 incorrectly restricted examples to resource.tf; supported resource*.tf variants are equally discoverable. Retain the example directory/provider prefix and require actual template inclusion. Found during independent review of the initial retained disposition.

The example directory/provider prefix and .tfquery.hcl extension are generator requirements. The original E1 incorrectly excluded supported list-resource*.tfquery.hcl variants; allow these without accepting .tf files or manual generated-doc edits. Found during independent review of the initial retained disposition.

The navigation brief does not mandate shareable tabs or task panels, and N4 already permits an intentional trade-off. Require a coherent explicit URL/history/reload/sharing contract and preserve any accepted one; do not silently demand additional shareability.
